title: Safetywashing: Do AI Safety Benchmarks Actually Measure Safety Progress?
summary: Meta-analysis of safety benchmarks: extracts a capabilities score (first principal component of 12 capability benchmarks) and training-compute estimates for dozens of chat and base models, then computes Spearman correlations between each safety benchmark and capabilities. Alignment/preference benchmarks (MT-Bench, Chatbot Arena), TruthfulQA, scalable-oversight datasets (GPQA, QuALITY), ETHICS and static adversarial robustness correlate highly with capabilities; bias benchmarks, MACHIAVELLI, jailbreak/GCG robustness and RMS calibration error do not; sycophancy and WMDP weaponization knowledge are anticorrelated. Recommends that new safety benchmarks report their capabilities correlation.
setting: 26 chat/instruct and 27 base language models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma, Falcon etc.), plus 63 adversarially trained and 44 standard vision models; Spearman correlations with a PCA capabilities score and with training FLOP. Fulltext re-extracted in this repo from the same arXiv HTML with math alt-text kept, so the correlation values appear in the text.

quotes.quote: Step 2: We extract the first principal component of the capabilities benchmarks and use it to compute a capabilities score for each model. Step 3: We identify whether safety benchmarks have high capabilities correlations using Spearman’s correlation.

While a high correlation indicates that a safety benchmark is measuring capabilities as a latent upstream factor—and is thus prone to safetywashing—a low correlation does not necessarily speak to the quality of the benchmark.
Old school attacks and natural adversarial examples seem to be highly correlated with capabilities, while jailbreaks and gradient-based methods like GCG are not.
Across vision and chat language models, we find that while the Brier Score calibration metric is highly correlated with accuracy, RMS calibration error is not.

In some cases, safety-related areas may act a jangle for capabilities; jangle fallacy is the erroneous belief that two constructs are different because they have the different names, when in practice they measure the same latent factor.
We do not cover transparency, anomaly detection, trojans, and other safety areas that do not have well-established preexisting benchmarks.

AI safety subfields such as alignment, scalable oversight, truthfulness, and static adversarial robustness are highly correlated with upstream general capabilities; areas such as bias, dynamic adversarial robustness, and calibration have relatively low correlations; measurements of sycophancy and weaponization risk have significant negative correlations with general capabilities.
Alignment evaluations largely measure upstream model capabilities and compute investment; as a goal to guide model development, alignment metrics are very similar to other capabilities benchmarks.
In chat models, performance on TruthfulQA seems to be a rebrand for accuracy (as reported in industry labs).

key_numbers.claim: Roughly half of the safety benchmarks studied correlate with capabilities.
key_numbers.quote: Our analysis reveals that many AI safety benchmarks—around half—often inadvertently capture latent factors closely tied to general capabilities and raw training compute, opening the door to safetywashing.

key_numbers.claim: Compute estimates available for 21 of 26 chat models.
Preference-alignment benchmarks: MT-Bench capabilities correlation 78.7%, compute 79.8%; Chatbot Arena 62.1% and 61.5% (Table 2).
Correlations below 40% treated as low; mean correlation among capability benchmarks 67.5%.
key_numbers.quote: We treat correlations below 40% as a low correlation.

key_numbers.claim: TruthfulQA MC1: capabilities correlation 81.2%, compute 83.1% (chat models).
key_numbers.quote: TruthfulQA MC1 has a capabilities correlation of 81.2% and compute correlation of 83.1% for chat models.

key_numbers.claim: Sycophancy correlates negatively with capabilities (-66.8%), MACHIAVELLI -49.9%, ETHICS +82.2%.
Jailbreak robustness is not positively correlated with capabilities (human jailbreaks -31.4%, TAP -42.8%, GCG -28.4%).
WMDP weaponization-knowledge safety scores anticorrelate with capabilities (bio -87.5%).

limitations_stated: A low correlation does not validate a benchmark's quality; areas without established benchmarks (transparency, anomaly detection, trojans) are not covered; the analysis is correlational across a model population and depends on which models are included.
open_questions: Correlations are computed across a cross-section of 2023-2024 open models; whether the same benchmarks stay capability-correlated for frontier models, agentic safety benchmarks and newer alignment evals (scheming, sabotage) is not measured. The method also cannot say whether a decorrelated benchmark measures the intended safety construct.
sense_of_alignment: Operator-goal and human-preference alignment as operationalized by benchmarks: 'Alignment refers to how well AI systems follow the goals of their operators', measured by helpfulness or instruction-following benchmarks (MT-Bench, Chatbot Arena), which the paper finds largely track capabilities.
